_note:
Slots for [brg_our-restaurants-brands]. Declared beside the fragment so a slot and its {token} ship in one commit. Generated into website/acf/ by `python3 kit/build-acf.py`; never hand-edit an acf.json. Slot names are underscore-only. Defaults are esc_html'd on fill, so write literal characters — a literal `&` and a literal `—`, never `&` or `—`.

Slots are NAMED PER BRAND (`bnb_*`, `odies_*`), deliberately not numbered `brand_1_*`/`brand_2_*`. Numbering would imply a repeater whose length is content, and it isn't: each plate carries its own brand lockup artwork, so a third brand is a BUILD task (new asset, new plate) rather than a content edit. Naming them says that. Same reasoning as home-about's vision/mission — two named things, not two rows.

The brand lockup plates deliberately have NO image reveal: the 2->1.2 counter-scale was cropping the wordmarks, and a brand mark should not be cropped for an effect (2026-08-10). They keep a plain fade-up, and that stays as code.

_baseline.why: Sean 2026-08-13 ruled the canonical name carries the Co. — odies_heading went from Odie's Pizza to Odie's Pizza Co. A deliberate approved copy change, verified rendering on one line.

bnb_heading.label: Board & Brew — name
bnb_heading.doc: The brand name. Write `&` as a literal ampersand.

bnb_body_1.label: Board & Brew — first paragraph
bnb_body_1.default: San Diego's iconic sandwich shop. Board & Brew has been handcrafting sandos with fresh-baked bread and premium ingredients since before craft sandwiches were cool.

bnb_body_2.label: Board & Brew — second paragraph
bnb_body_2.doc: Carries the live location count, so it needs editing whenever that changes. Write `—` as a literal em dash. CROSS-SECTION FACT — this number also appears in `home-community` -> Body copy second paragraph, and `community-stats` -> Stat 1 figure. Going ACF-editable REMOVED the check that used to catch a mismatch: it was three greppable strings in the repo, and it is now three database rows that nothing repo-side can compare. If you change one, change all three. (`doc` strings are per-field by construction, so this warning has to be repeated in each — there is nowhere on this project that can hold a cross-section fact.)
bnb_body_2.default: 12 locations across San Diego and Orange County — each one a neighborhood staple.

bnb_cta_href.label: Board & Brew — button link
bnb_cta_href.doc: Opens in a new tab; target/rel are in the markup.

odies_heading.label: Odie's — name
odies_heading.doc: The brand name. CANONICAL FORM — Sean 2026-08-13: the official name carries the Co. at the end. Body copy is deliberately NOT swept to match; he asked that prose follow whatever copy is provided, and both forms are in use interchangeably. So this field is the one place the official name is asserted — change it here, leave the paragraphs alone.

odies_body_1.label: Odie's — first paragraph
odies_body_1.doc: Write `—` as a literal em dash.
odies_body_1.default: Oceanside's newest pizza obsession. Odie's Pizza Co. brings sourdough pies and radical vibes to the Southern California coast — think big slices, bold flavors, and a neighborhood vibe that makes you want to stick around.

odies_body_2.label: Odie's — second paragraph
odies_body_2.doc: Says more locations are coming, so it will need editing when they land.
odies_body_2.default: Our flagship is right in the heart of downtown Oceanside, and more locations are on the way.

odies_cta_href.label: Odie's — button link
odies_cta_href.doc: Opens in a new tab; target/rel are in the markup.

bnb_image.label: Board & Brew — image
bnb_image.doc: The artwork in the Board & Brew panel. Landscape, around 800x550. An SVG logo lockup or a photo both work. Leave empty to keep the current picture.

bnb_image_tone.label: Board & Brew — image — color
bnb_image_tone.doc: Color is the default. Switch this photo to black and white when you want it that way on purpose — the photography on this site was only ever gray because the placeholder images were. Affects this photo alone.

bnb_image_px.label: Board & Brew — image — movement
bnb_image_px.doc: How far this photo drifts inside its frame as you scroll, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off. The dropdown this replaces offered 6, 10 and 16 as Subtle, Medium and Strong, so anything already set still reads exactly the same — you can now pick the values in between. 40 is the ceiling: the page itself stops there, so a larger number would do nothing. The photo is laid out taller than its frame and slides within it, so an edge never appears and it is never zoomed.

bnb_image_px_dir.label: Board & Brew — image — movement direction
bnb_image_px_dir.doc: Which way this photo travels as the page scrolls. Neighboring photos set in opposite directions are what reads as depth.

odies_image.doc: The artwork in the Odie's panel. Landscape, around 800x550. Leave empty to keep the current picture.

odies_image_tone.label: Odie's — image — color

section_bg.label: Section background
section_bg.doc: A pattern or photo filling this whole section, behind everything else. Leave it empty — as it is now — and the section keeps the plain color it has today; nothing changes until you choose something. It is cropped to fill, so the exact size does not matter. ON A DARK SECTION USE A LIGHT OR GRAY ARTWORK: a black pattern over a black panel stays invisible however high you set the strength below.

section_bg_opacity.label: Background strength
section_bg_opacity.doc: How strongly the background shows through. Choose 100% when the artwork already has the intended strength built into the file — anything lower then fades a graphic that was supplied ready to use. Use the lower values when a full-strength image would compete with the words in front of it.

section_bg_px.label: Background movement
section_bg_px.doc: Drifts the background as the page scrolls, behind the content, as a percentage of the section's height. 0 is off — the right starting point, because a pattern moving too fast pulls the eye away from the copy. 6 is subtle, 10 medium, 16 strong, and anything in between is allowed. 40 is the ceiling; the page stops there.

section_bg_px_dir.label: Background movement direction
section_bg_px_dir.doc: Which way the background travels as the page scrolls. Only matters once movement above is above 0. Neighboring sections set in opposite directions are what reads as depth rather than as one sheet sliding.

section_bg_mobile.label: Section background — phones
section_bg_mobile.doc: Optional. A version of the background for phones, used below 768px wide. Leave it empty and the main background above is used at every size. Worth setting when the main artwork is wide: cropped to a narrow screen it often shows nothing recognizable, and a tall or simplified version reads far better.

mark_1_ast_art.label: Artwork
mark_1_ast_art.doc: Which mark is drawn here. Leave it alone to keep the one the design uses. Any SVG or PNG from the media library works; SVG stays crisp at any size.

mark_1_ast_pos.label: Position
mark_1_ast_pos.doc: Where the mark sits in its section. "Where the design put it" is the starting point and leaves it exactly where it is now — choose one of the nine only when you want to move it. Corners sit inside the section padding, so a long headline cannot push a mark down into the type.

mark_1_ast_opacity.label: Opacity
mark_1_ast_opacity.doc: How solid the mark is. 100 is as drawn; lower settles it into the background.

mark_1_ast_show.label: Show this mark
mark_1_ast_show.doc: Hiding removes just this one mark. Nothing else in the section changes.

mark_1_ast_anim.label: Animation
mark_1_ast_anim.doc: How the mark moves. "As built" keeps what it does today — a hard-cut jitter for most, a spin for the asterisk in the hero cluster. Still stops it entirely. Anyone who has switched off animation in their system settings sees it still whatever is chosen here.

btn_color.label: Button color
btn_color.doc: The button's color. "As designed" is the starting point and leaves this section's buttons exactly as they look today — which matters, because several sections paint theirs black on purpose and the give-back slider alternates yellow and black down the slides. Choose a color and it takes over. The words flip to black or white automatically, whichever reads on the color you pick. This applies to every button in this section.

btn_style.label: Filled or outline
btn_style.doc: Filled is a solid block of color. Outline draws the color as a ring with the words in it and nothing behind — useful over a photo, where a solid block can sit heavily. "As designed" leaves it as it is today, which is filled everywhere. Both are exactly the same size, so switching one does not move anything around it.

btn_effect.label: Hover effect
btn_effect.doc:
What the button does when someone points at it. Lift is what every button has always done and stays the default — it rises slightly and casts a shadow. Lift and swap color does that AND flips to the opposite ink, which is the loudest of the set and best kept for one main action on a page. Underline draws a rule under the words and leaves the button still, which reads as a link — a good fit for the small buttons. Grow swells it in place. Press down pushes it into the page. Fill in floods an outline button with its color, so pair it with Outline. None holds it still.

This is the HOVER only; the way the button arrives on screen is the site-wide reveal. Anyone who has switched off animation sees no hover movement whatever is chosen.

buttons.label: Buttons
buttons.doc:
Buttons for this section. Add as many as you need — they sit in a row and wrap onto the next line on a narrow screen. Leave the list empty, as it is now, and the section has no buttons at all and looks exactly as it does today.

Their color, fill and hover come from Button style below and apply to all of them.

label.label: Label
label.doc: The words on the button. Short reads best: it is set in capitals with wide letter spacing. A button with no label is not drawn.

href.label: Link
href.doc: Where it goes. A path like /careers/ stays on this site, a full address goes off it, and mailto:someone@blacktoprg.com opens a mail window.

popup.label: Open in a pop-up
popup.doc: For a Google Form, choose Pop-up and it opens in a panel over the page instead of sending people to Google. A form that is set to require a Google sign-in CANNOT be shown this way — Google's sign-in page refuses to be embedded and the panel comes up blank — so that one has to stay on Open the link until its Responses settings are changed. Anything that is not a form stays on Open the link.

cta_position.label: Where the buttons sit
cta_position.doc: At the bottom is the usual place and the one the rest of the site uses. This section has no heading, so the bottom is the only position offered.

choices.foot: At the bottom of the section

modal_bg.label: Pop-up background
modal_bg.doc: The color of the panel a form opens in. Match it to the form's own Theme color in Google Forms and the two read as one surface. This cannot color the form itself — that is Google's page on Google's domain.
